**My reasoning:**

I am 75 years old and I have farmed this land in Quzhou my whole life. My back is not what it used to be, and two of my three children are in the city now. I farm about 5 mu — I gave up some contracted land a few years ago because it was too much for me.

There is nothing to think about regarding what to grow. I grow winter wheat, then summer corn. Same as my father did. Same as everyone here does. The land here is flat and the soil is good for grain. I know this rotation. I know when to water and when to spray. I am not going to try vegetables or cotton at my age — that is too much trouble and too much risk.

For wheat, I will use the Jimai seed the village cooperative sells. It yields well and it does not lodge in wind. I plant in early October. I will water three times — once before it gets cold to help it root, once at jointing, once at heading. I put down compound fertilizer at planting and urea when the plants start to joint. I spray twice — once for powdery mildew in spring, once for aphids near heading. I use rotary tillage before planting because my neighbor rents his machine out cheaply.

After wheat harvest in June, I plant corn directly into the stubble. No-tillage saves me effort. I use Zhengdan 958 — I have used it for fifteen years and it never disappoints me. Summer rain here usually takes care of the water, but if August is dry I will pump once. One pesticide spray for corn borer. Corn comes off in late September and then the cycle starts again.

I do not measure my fertilizer precisely. I go by what I have always used and what my neighbors use. I apply a little more nitrogen than the extension office says because my yields feel better that way.

Rotary tillage precedes wheat planting but maize is sown no-till directly into wheat stubble to save labor. The plan prioritizes simplicity, physical manageability, and known outcomes over optimization or experimentation."
